([[Randallstown, Maryland]]) | college = *[[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] (2004–2006) *[[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] (2007–2009) | draft_year = 2009 | career_start = 2009 | career_end = 2019 | years1 = 2009–2010 | team1 = [[Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi S.K.|Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi]] | years2 = 2010 | team2 = [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] | years3 = 2010–2011 | team3 = [[Austin Toros]] | years4 = {{nbay|2010|end}} | team4 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years5 = 2011 | team5 = [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | years6 = 2012 | team6 = [[Guaiqueríes de Margarita]] | years7 = 2012 | team7 = Caneros de La Romana | years8 = 2012–2013 | team8 = [[Kyoto Hannaryz]] | years9 = 2013–2015 | team9 = [[BC Krasny Oktyabr|Krasny Oktyabr Volgograd]] | years10 = 2015 | team10 = [[Caciques de Humacao]] | years11 = 2015 | team11 = [[Blackwater Elite]] | years12 = 2015–2016 | team12 = [[Shinshu Brave Warriors]] | years13 = 2017 | team13 = [[Gunma Crane Thunders]] | years14 = 2018 | team14 = [[Sendai 89ers]] | years15 = 2018–2019 | team15 = [[Iwate Big Bulls]] | highlights = * [[NBA D-League All-Star]] ([[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2011]]) * [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League Second Team]] ([[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2011]]) * [[NBA D-League]] All-Defensive Second Team ([[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2011]]) * [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Ligat HaAl]] champion (2010) }} '''Marcus Lynn Cousin Jr.''' (pronounced '''coo-ZON'''; born December 18, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Seton Hall University]] and the [[University of Houston]]. ==High school career== Cousin attended [[Randallstown High School]] in [[Randallstown, Maryland]]. During his junior season, he averaged 14 points and 7 rebounds per game. He also participated in the Charm City Classic All-Star game. During his senior season, he averaged 11 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks per game before sitting out the final two months with an ankle injury.[http://www.uhcougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cousin_marcus01.html 50 Marcus Cousin] Michigan State, Nebraska, USC and Massachusetts were all interested in Cousin, but he eventually decided to sign with Seton Hall. ==College career== In his freshman season at [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], Cousin played sparingly. In 18 games (no starts), he averaged 0.4 points and 1.1 rebounds in 6 minutes per game. In his sophomore season, he helped the Pirates to an 18–12 record and a berth in the NCAA Tournament against [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]]. In 26 games (13 starts), he averaged 2.1 points and 3.5 rebounds in 13.1 minutes per game. In 2006, he transferred to the [[University of Houston]]. Due to NCAA transfer rules, he was forced to sit out the 2006–07 season. In his redshirted junior season at [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], he finished third on the team in blocks with 22. In 29 games (no starts), he averaged 4.4 points and 4.0 rebounds in 13.8 minutes per game. In his senior season, he had his best year of college basketball. In 33 games (32 starts), he averaged 10.9 points, 8.4 rebounds and 2.1 blocks in 30 minutes per game. ==Professional career== ===2009–10 season=== After going undrafted in the [[2009 NBA draft]], Cousin joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the 2009 [[NBA Summer League]]. He later signed with [[Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi S.K.|Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi]] in Turkey for the 2009–10 season. In January 2010, he left Turkey and signed with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] in Israel for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/79688/marcus-cousin-moves-to-gilboa-galil.html Marcus Cousin moves to Gilboa Galil] ===2010–11 season=== On September 27, 2010, Cousin signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. However, he was later waived by the Spurs on October 22, 2010.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6707 Spurs waive Marcus Cousin] On October 30, 2010, he was acquired by the [[Austin Toros]] as an affiliate player. On March 9, 2011, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/cousin_110309.html Austin's Marcus Cousin Signs With Utah Jazz] On March 19, 2011, he returned to the Toros. On April 11, 2011, he signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] for the rest of the season[http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/cousin_signs_with_houston_2011_04_11.html Austin's Marcus Cousin Signs with Houston] and was immediately assigned to the Rio Grande Valley Vipers.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/cousin_110411.html Rockets Assign Marcus Cousin To Vipers][http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets_sign_cousin__recall_2011_04_11.html Rockets Sign Cousin, Recall Thabeet] On May 1, 2011, he returned to the Rockets following the conclusion of the NBA D-League season. On December 24, 2011, he was waived by the Rockets before the start of the [[2011–12 NBA season]]. He did not appear in a game for the Rockets during his tenure. ===2012 off-season=== In March 2012, Cousin signed with [[Guaiqueríes de Margarita]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]] in Venezuela for the 2012 LPB season. However, he left after one game. In July 2012, he joined the NBA D-League Select Team for the 2012 NBA Summer League.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/summerleague/bio/marcus_cousin.html NBA Development League: 2012 Select Team Bio: Marcus Cousin] In August 2012, he signed with Caneros de La Romana in the Dominican Republic for a short stint. ===2012–13 season=== In September 2012, Cousin signed with [[Kyoto Hannaryz]] of the [[bj league]] for the 2012–13 season.{{cite news |title=Kyoto signs ex-NBA center Cousin |url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2012/09/05/sports/kyoto-signs-ex-nba-center-cousin/ |work=[[The Japan Times]]|date=September 5, 2012 |access-date=June 4, 2015}} In 57 games, he averaged 14.5 points and 9.7 rebounds per game. ===2013–14 season=== On September 30, 2013, Cousin signed with the San Antonio Spurs.[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/130930_spurs_training_camp_roster Spurs Announce Training Camp Roster] However, he was later waived by the Spurs on October 15, 2013.[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131015_spurs_waive_cousin_kabongo_maggette Spurs Waive Cousin, Kabongo and Maggette] On November 27, 2013, he signed with [[BC Krasny Oktyabr|Krasny Oktyabr Volgograd]] of Russia for the rest of the 2013–14 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/vtb-league/108613/marcus-cousin-moves-to-krasny-oktyabr.html Marcus Cousin moves to Krasny Oktyabr] ===2014–15 season=== On August 17, 2014, Cousin re-signed with Krasny Oktyabr on a one-year deal.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/131764/marcus-cousin-re-signs-with-krasny-oktyabr.html Marcus Cousin re-signs with Krasny Oktyabr] On March 1, 2015, he parted ways with Krasny Oktyabr.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/153949/krasny-oktyabr-cuts-marcus-cousin.html Krasny Oktyabr cuts Marcus Cousin] On April 5, 2015, he signed with [[Caciques de Humacao]] of the Puerto Rican [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/157512/caciques-de-humacao-land-marcus-cousin.html Caciques de Humacao land Marcus Cousin] He left Humacao later that month after appearing in eight games for the club. On June 4, he signed with the [[Blackwater Elite]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] for the rest of the [[2015 PBA Governors' Cup]] as a replacement for [[Marcus Douthit]].{{cite news |last=Dy | first=Richard |title=Marcus Cousin – no relation to DeMarcus Cousins – to step in for Douthit at Blackwater |url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/new-blackwater-import-marcus-cousins-marcus-douthit-pba-replacement-governors-cup-dioceldo-sy |work=Spin.ph |date=June 4, 2015 |access-date=June 4, 2015}} ===2015–16 season=== In September 2015, Cousin signed with the [[Shinshu Brave Warriors]] for the 2015–16 [[bj league]] season.{{cite news |last=Odeven | first=Ed |title=Well-traveled Cousin joins Brave Warriors |url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2015/09/17/basketball/bj-league/well-traveled-cousin-joins-brave-warriors/#.Vp-pCMB94zY |work=JapanTimes.co.jp |date=September 17, 2015 |access-date=January 20, 2016}} He left the team in January 2016 after appearing in 12 games. ===2016–17 season=== In October 2016, Cousin signed with [[Hekmeh BC|Sagesse]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].{{cite news |last=Mawloud | first=Maarouf |title=Marcus Cousin inks with sagesse |url=http://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/466300/Marcus-Cousin-inks-with-sagesse |work=Asia-basket.com |date=October 18, 2016 |access-date=October 18, 2016}} He left before playing in a game for them. In January 2017, he joined Japanese team [[Gunma Crane Thunders]]. In 30 games, he averaged 10.6 points, 8.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game. ===2017–18 season=== On January 17, 2018, Cousin signed with [[Sendai 89ers]], returning to Japan for a fourth stint.{{cite web|url=https://www.89ers.jp/news/38681.html|title=[お知らせ] マーカス･クザン選手 選手契約締結のお知らせ|work=89ers.jp|date=January 17, 2018|access-date=January 17, 2018|language=Japanese}} ===2018–19 season=== In December 2018, Cousin joined the [[Iwate Big Bulls]], returning to Japan for a fifth stint.{{cite
